clue.text: Dictators perhaps powerful at ending those lives?

parts.note: potent means powerful

indicators.note: ending asks for the closing letter of each of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A question about whether mighty rulers bring an end to the lives of their subjects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending' takes the last letters of 'those' and 'lives', giving E and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Rulers holding absolute power, such as autocrats, are examples of monarchs and dictators alike, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Love the guys signal

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O
the guys are men

explanation.surface: A romantic gesture aimed at a group of blokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign or portent foretelling events is a signal of what is to come.

clue.text: It's no longer wrong to screw someone?

parts.note: ex- means former, no longer
a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question suggesting cheating someone is no longer considered wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To screw money out of someone is slang for wringing it from them by threats or force.

clue.text: Instructs Blackbeard on a couple of small points

parts.note: Blackbeard was the pirate Edward Teach
two compass points, east and south, abbreviated E and S

explanation.surface: The pirate Blackbeard gives a lesson on a pair of minor details.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who educates pupils gives them lessons and instructs them.

clue.text: Neat but make shipshape

definitions.meaning: a verb, to put things in order

explanation.definitionFit: Orderly describes a neat room, and putting a room in order is to make it shipshape.

clue.text: Fully satisfied with journalist being tranquillised

indicators.note: with here means the first piece holds the second within it

parts.note: sated means fully satisfied
ED is short for editor, the stock crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter is calm and contented, perhaps after a good meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient given a calming drug has been tranquillised, put under sedation.

clue.text: The box set of olivenites

indicators.note: set suggests the letters are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A collection of olivenite mineral specimens displayed as a set.
explanation.walkthrough: Olivenite is a green copper mineral; 'set of' rearranges its plural's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The box is British slang for the TV set in the living room.

clue.text: Swift wind helps a bit with horses

parts.note: the swift is a bird closely resembling the martin, so one stands in for the other
a gale is a strong wind

explanation.surface: A fast breeze makes riding a little easier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swift' looks like an adjective meaning fast; here it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This harness strap stops a horse raising its head too high, so it is tack that helps a rider control the animal.

clue.text: Phoebe taking to Greek character

indicators.note: to here joins the run of letters across the two words to the character they hold

explanation.surface: A woman called Phoebe is learning the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The second letter of the Greek alphabet is a character of that script.

clue.text: Sinister to have port passed

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
handed means passed over

explanation.surface: A suggestion that passing the port is somehow sinister.
explanation.walkthrough: Port is traditionally passed to the left at British dinners, which drives the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister is Latin for left, and heraldry uses it for the left-hand side.

clue.text: Although it's what a vestment can tie up

parts.note: an alb is a white priest's vestment

indicators.note: in a down-reading sense, up means the word tie is read backwards

explanation.surface: A question about what a cleric's robe can be fastened with.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjunction meaning even though or though.

clue.text: Customary of Cumbrian river beds

parts.note: set means fixed, customary, as in set ways
the River Tees rises on Cross Fell in Cumbria, northern England

explanation.surface: Something traditional about the river beds of north-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'river beds' reads as one idea; 'beds' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Sofas, especially sofa-beds, are used to sleep on as beds.

clue.text: Drunkard entertains sailor with a gin to force wrecking

indicators.note: entertains means the drunkard holds the sailor inside

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard
AB, able-bodied seaman, a sailor
taken as written
g is the symbol for gravitational force

explanation.surface: A drunk hosts a sailor and uses gin to push for destruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately damaging or wrecking something is sabotage.

clue.text: Fruit produced by the argentines

indicators.note: produced by means the letters of the following word are reworked

explanation.surface: Fruit grown by Argentinians.
explanation.definitionFit: Small orange citrus fruits, related to the mandarin.

clue.text: Attempt to catch a young pig

indicators.note: to catch means the first word holds the letter inside it

parts.note: a shot is an attempt

explanation.surface: Trying to grab a piglet.
explanation.definitionFit: A recently weaned piglet is a young pig.

clue.text: Department of denomination I follow on

parts.note: a sect is a religious denomination
taken as written

explanation.surface: A church office where the speaker carries on after someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A division of an organisation, such as a department of a store.

clue.text: For example black Irish saint returns the chairs

parts.note: the Black Sea and the Irish Sea are examples of a sea

indicators.note: returns means the abbreviation is read backwards

explanation.surface: A dark Irish saint comes back to take his chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black Irish' tempts as stout; the Black and Irish are two seas.
explanation.definitionFit: Chairs are things to sit on.

clue.text: Reg starts in the hut ready to scrap

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the hut

parts.note: a shed is a hut

indicators.note: starts asks for the opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: Reg begins work in the shed, prepared to throw things out.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear up or scrap a document is to put it through a shredder.

clue.text: Disallow the final scourge

parts.note: to ban is to disallow

indicators.note: final asks for the closing letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Ruling out the last plague.
explanation.definitionFit: A persistent cause of trouble, a scourge or curse.

clue.text: Fiddle a city in Latvia

parts.note: to rig is to fiddle, as in a rigged result

explanation.surface: Fiddling with a Baltic capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' could be a violin; here it is to cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: Latvia's capital and largest city.

clue.text: Slacks but snap up in the beginning

indicators.note: in places that opening letter inside the turned word
up means the word snap is read backwards in this down-style sense
beginning asks for the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Trousers that suddenly tear right at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns 'snap' to PANS; 'in the beginning' puts T inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Trousers are slacks, especially in American use.

clue.text: Mimic in part of breastwork

indicators.note: in means the copycat goes inside the next word

parts.note: taken as written
to ape is to mimic

explanation.surface: Imitating part of a fortification.
explanation.definitionFit: A low protective wall, as on a rampart, is a breastwork.

clue.text: Disinfected the leister before use

indicators.note: before use suggests the fishing spear's letters are put into a new state, as a tool is cleaned

explanation.surface: Cleaning a fishing spear before using it.
explanation.walkthrough: A leister is a pronged fishing spear, chiefly Scottish.
explanation.definitionFit: Free from germs, having been disinfected.

clue.text: He ends in danger at that place

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the word for danger

parts.note: a threat is a danger

indicators.note: ends asks for the closing letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A man meets his end in peril at some spot.
explanation.definitionFit: An old formal adverb meaning there, at that point.

clue.text: Way the mountain looks odd

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: The path up a peak has a peculiar look.
explanation.definitionFit: Peculiar or odd things are unusual.

clue.text: Today split free

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era we live in today
a rift is a split

explanation.surface: Breaking away to freedom today.
explanation.definitionFit: Floating loose, cut free from moorings.

clue.text: A GI she dances with in Japan

definitions.text: A GI she dances with in Japan

indicators.note: dances suggests the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: An American soldier dancing with a woman in Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese hostess trained to entertain with dance and conversation, as a soldier might meet.

clue.text: Unfriendly for a party city

parts.note: a do is a party
Ur was an ancient city in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A grumpy attitude toward a city-wide celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern and gloomy, unfriendly in manner.

clue.text: Love to set fire to a small stream

definitions.meaning: a Scottish and northern word for a brook

explanation.walkthrough: 'Love to' is linking surface; one may also read it as a third sense, to be consumed by passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting alight is to ignite; a brook in Scotland is called by the same short word.

clue.text: Colossal reminder soldier was in debt

parts.note: a prod is a nudge or reminder

indicators.note: was in means the soldier is placed inside the debts

parts.note: IOUs are notes of debt
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A huge reminder that a soldier owed money.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormous or colossal, remarkably great in size.

clue.text: Formerly party leader is a turnip

parts.note: nee means formerly called, of a maiden name

indicators.note: leader asks for the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A former party leader is called a turnip.
explanation.walkthrough: A neep is the Scottish word for a turnip or swede.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots name for a swede or turnip, served with haggis.

clue.text: Is Peru intent on becoming thinner

indicators.note: becoming means the letters change into something new

explanation.surface: Is Peru set on growing slimmer?
explanation.definitionFit: A solvent used to thin paint, a thinner.
